subject: Deployment decision: TLS split-point for private runtime (ingress-proxy vs runtime mTLS)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, security@archimedes-corp.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: where to terminate TLS for Archimedes private deployment

Hi Karthik / Archimedes security team,

Following yesterday's call I put together a short proposal that lays out two architecture options for TLS termination in the Archimedes private deployment:

1) Terminate TLS at their ingress proxy (customer-managed) and use mutual TLS between their proxy and our runtime over the VPC peering.
2) Terminate TLS at our runtime (we manage certs for the private host) and rely on split-horizon DNS pointing the private domain to our internal endpoints; customer terminates at their edge only for external traffic.

Attached is a one-page comparison (tls-decision-proposal.pdf) and a sample k8s/network snippet (archimedes-network-draft.yaml). High-level asks:
- Archimedes: confirm whether they can host an ingress proxy with a wildcard cert and support mTLS to our runtime, or prefer us to take termination inside their VPC.
- Internal: we need SRE + Security input on failure modes, cert rotation, and auditability for both options.

Notes: latency requirement is 50ms p95; Archimedes wants minimal cross-team ops on their side.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0187

Attachments: tls-decision-proposal.pdf, archimedes-network-draft.yaml
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: security@archimedes-corp.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: where to terminate TLS for Archimedes private deployment

Jonas — thanks for the write-up and the attachment. I skimmed both options and here are SRE's practical notes: 

- Option 1 (terminate at customer proxy + mTLS to runtime):
  * Pros: customer retains full control of public CA certs and DNS; our runtime only needs to validate client certs. Rotation responsibilities sit with the customer for edge certs, but we must handle the mTLS cert lifecycle for the runtime.
  * Cons: introduces an extra mTLS hop which complicates debugging and increases management surface (client certs distribution). Need an onboarding playbook for Archimedes' infra team.

- Option 2 (we terminate TLS at runtime):
  * Pros: simpler from our operations standpoint — single cert lifecycle to manage for customer traffic; easier logs/tracing correlation.
  * Cons: customer may object to us holding certs for their private domain; requires split-horizon DNS and tighter network isolation. Also increases audit burden (we must prove cert handling meets their compliance).

Operational concerns common to both:
- Cert rotation automation (ACME vs KMS-backed): prefer a KMS/HSM-backed rotation if we keep certs.
- Monitoring: need tokenized tracing to preserve customer PII constraints.
- Failover: define clear fallback route if mTLS handshake fails (return 502 vs fallback to public endpoint).

I'll draft a short onboarding checklist for Option 1 if Archimedes can host the proxy. If they can't, we'll need a documented audit trail for Option 2.

-grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: where to terminate TLS for Archimedes private deployment

Team — quick summary and recommended path so we can get Archimedes onboarded this month.

Summary of constraints from Archimedes call:
- They can run an ingress proxy but want zero-op changes after cutover.
- Their compliance team requires proof of cert rotations and scoped access to private keys.
- Network latency budget: 50ms p95; they prefer avoiding extra hops.

Recommendation (single path to accelerate rollout):
1) Default to Option 1: customer-terminates at their ingress proxy + mTLS to our runtime, with the following guardrails:
   - We provide an agent + small onboarding script to provision client certs for the proxy and rotate them automatically every 90 days.
   - We require Archimedes to supply a wildcard cert for public-facing hostnames (they manage public CA).
   - We will run healthchecks and a canary for mTLS for 72 hours before flipping production traffic.
2) Fallback/Alternative: If Archimedes refuses to host an ingress proxy, we will accept delegated cert custody under strict KMS/HSM controls and an audit SLA (Option 2).

Action items:
- Jonas: confirm Archimedes can install the onboarding agent (due 2026-02-18).
- Karthik/Grace: finalize the rotation automation script and the canary playbook (due 2026-02-20).
- Hiro: sign off on the audit checklist and any encryption controls required if we hold certs.

I'll take ownership of the rollout plan and the stakeholder communications.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: where to terminate TLS for Archimedes private deployment (sign-off)

Marissa / team — I reviewed the proposed guardrails and am comfortable with the recommended default (Option 1) provided we implement the following mandatory security controls before production traffic: 

- KMS-backed client certs for our runtime; private keys never leave HSM.
- Signed rotation logs retained for a minimum of 1 year and shared with Archimedes via a read-only audit feed.
- mTLS mutual authentication with pinning of Issuer DN and a defined rollback plan.
- Short-lived cert TTL (<= 90 days) and immediate revocation path documented in the runbook.

Once Karthik/Grace confirm the automation is in place, I sign off and we can proceed with Jonas' customer onboarding. Also copy of confluence page with decision stored here: https://confluence.redwood.ai/infra/tls-splitpoint-decision-2026

-Hiro
